The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no. 156/2013 registered at Police Station Hari Nagar, New Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 420/468/471/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.

sentences.text: 2. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Pawan Jain and Investigating Officer (IO), Police Station, Hari Nagar, New Delhi.

3. The brief facts of the case are that petitioner no. 1 and respondent nos. 2 & 3 herein are close family members as respondent no. 2 is mother of the petitioner no. 1 and the respondent no. 3 is real sister of the petitioner no. l.

The father of the petitioner no. l and the respondent no. 3 i.e.
husband of the respondent no. 2 herein expired on 04.10.2009, after which some disputes and differences arose between petitioner no. l and the respondents no. 2 & 3.

As a result thereof, the respondents no. 2 & 3 herein lodged police complaints against the petitioners and thereafter, filed a complaint case under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. before the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, West District, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi seeking directions for registration of an FIR for the offences punishable under Sections 420/468/471/34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 against the petitioners on the allegations that after the death of Sh. Subhash Chand Bhalla, the petitioner no. l being elder son of the family took all the documents of all properties, fix deposits receipts of bank, passbook and jewellery of the family in his custody that were left by Late Sh. Subhash Chand Bhalla with the intention to deprive other family members for their due shares.

sentences.text: 1 petitioner no. 2, got installed new electricity connection in his name at the property bearing no. B-7 9, Hari Nagar, New Delhi-110064 and prayed for registration of a criminal case against the petitioners.
During pendency of the abovesaid complaint, FIR bearing no. 156/2013 under Sections 420/468/471/34 of IPG was registered against the petitioners at P.S. Hari Nagar, Delhi.

During trial of the abovesaid complaint case, the petitioners and the respondent nos. 2 & 3 with the intervention of their elder family members, relatives and respectable persons of the society amicably resolved all their disputes, differences and claims against each other and decided to live peacefully in future.
The petitioners and respondent nos. 2 & 3 entered into a Compromise Deed with respect to their amicable settlement.

4. On a query made by this Court, respondent nos. 2 & 3 who have been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that they have entered into compromise out of their own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent nos. 2 & 3 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between them.
Respondent nos. 2 & 3 further stated that they have no objection if FIR may be quashed.

5. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings

,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would, thus, be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

6. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 156/2013 registered at Police Station Hari Nagar, New Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 420/468/471/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
